topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening framing introduces the lecture, outlines the themes of cancer evolution and the microenvironment, and states the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumor development is driven by Darwinian selection of advantageous somatic mutations and complementary non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cancer stem cells and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between normal tissue hierarchies and tumorigenesis, evaluating theoretical models and experimental evidence for cancer stem cells and cells of origin in leukemia and colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Microenvironmental, inflammatory, and stromal influences on cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how microenvironmental signals, chronic inflammation, and supportive stroma promote tumor growth and provide avenues for microenvironment-targeted therapies.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the sequencing, modeling, and spatial profiling technologies used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Integrative synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how mutational accumulation, cell-of-origin properties, and microenvironmental context collectively drive cancer development as an evolutionary process.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The closing framing concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the next lecture.
